PART I
Item 1.    Business
Company Background
Acme Devices, Inc. (“Acme” or the “Company”) designs, manufactures and markets industrial sensors, controllers and related software. The Company’s fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. The Company was incorporated in Delaware in 1987 and is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio.
The Company sells its products through its direct sales force, distributors and online stores in more than 40 countries. For a discussion of risks that could affect the business, see Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K under the heading “Risk Factors.”
Products
The Company’s principal products are the Vector line of pressure sensors, the Atlas line of programmable controllers and the Beacon monitoring software. Net sales of Vector sensors were 1,204 million in 2023.
Human Capital
As of September 30, 2023, the Company had approximately 12,400 full-time equivalent employees. The Company believes its culture of engineering excellence is a key competitive advantage.

Item 1A.    Risk Factors
The Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including those described below.
Macroeconomic and Industry Risks
The Company depends on a limited number of suppliers for key components, and supply disruptions could materially harm its business.
Many components used in the Company’s sensors are obtained from single or limited sources. Global semiconductor shortages in recent years have increased lead times and component costs. If a supplier fails to deliver on time, the Company may be unable to meet customer demand, and its net sales and gross margin could decline. The Company also relies on contract manufacturers located primarily in Mexico and Malaysia.
Global economic conditions could materially adversely affect the Company.
Demand for industrial equipment is cyclical. Adverse economic conditions, including inflation, higher interest rates and slower industrial production, could cause customers to delay or cancel orders. A significant portion of the Company’s net sales comes from customers in the energy and manufacturing sectors, which are especially sensitive to the economic cycle.

Legal and Regulatory Risks
The Company is subject to complex and changing laws and regulations worldwide.
The Company’s operations are subject to export controls, environmental rules, data privacy laws and anti-corruption laws. Changes to tariffs or trade restrictions, particularly between the U.S. and China, could increase the Company’s costs or limit its ability to sell products in certain markets. Compliance failures could result in fines, penalties or reputational harm.

Item 1B.    Unresolved Staff Comments
None.
Item 1C.    Cybersecurity
The Company maintains a cybersecurity risk management program overseen by the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors. The Chief Information Security Officer reports to the Audit Committee quarterly.
Item 2.    Properties
The Company’s headquarters are located in Columbus, Ohio. The Company owns manufacturing facilities in Ohio and Texas.
Item 3.    Legal Proceedings
The Company is subject to a patent infringement lawsuit filed by Sensorium LLC in the Eastern District of Texas in March 2023. The Company believes the claims are without merit and intends to defend itself vigorously.
Item 4.    Mine Safety Disclosures
Not applicable.

Item 7.    Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K.
Fiscal 2023 Highlights
Total net sales decreased 3% or $95 million during 2023 compared to 2022, driven primarily by lower sales of Atlas controllers, partially offset by higher sales of Beacon software subscriptions.

Liquidity and Capital Resources
As of September 30, 2023, the Company had $812 million of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. The Company believes its balances will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements over the next 12 months.

Item 7A.    Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
The Company is exposed to interest rate risk on its investment portfolio and foreign currency risk, primarily from the euro and the Mexican peso. A hypothetical 10% strengthening of the U.S. dollar would have reduced net sales by approximately $41 million in 2023.
